lg.l: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain and the other is the cure thereof.

div.p: [kuṟippu aṟital] aḵtāvatu talaimakan talaimakaḷ kuṟippiṉai aṟitalum tōḻi kuṟippiṉai aṟitalum, avaḷtāṉ avviruvar kuṟippiṉaiyum aṟitalumām. takaiyaṇaṅkuṟṟa talaimakan talaimakaḷaik kūṭuṅkāl itu vēṇṭumākaliṉ, takaiyaṇaṅkuṟuttaliṉpiṉ vaikkappaṭṭatu.
[This section is called "Praise of the Deity"]—
(itaṉporuḷ) talaimakan talaimakaḷ uḷappāṭṭukkuṟippiṉai avaḷ ṉōkkiṉāṉ aṟintatu.
The meaning of this [Kuṟaḷ]

ivaḷ uṇkaṇ uḷḷatu irunōkku - ivaḷuṭaiya uṇkaṇakattatāya nōkku itupoḻutu eṉmēl iraṇṭu nōkkāyiṟṟu ; orunōkku nōynōkku oṉṟu annōy maruntu - avaṟṟuḷ orunōkku eṉkaṇ nōy ceyyumnōkku. ēṉaiyatu annōykku maruntāya nōkku eṉṟavāṟu. uṇkaṇ - maiyuṇṭa kaṇ. nōyceyyum nōkku avaḷ maṉattiṉāya kāmakkuṟippiṉai veḷippaṭukkiṉṟa nōkku. maruntāya nōkkut taṉkaṇ nikaḻkiṉra aṉpu nōkku. nōyceyyum nōkkiṉaip potunōkku eṉpārum uḷar ; atu nōyceyiṉ kaikkiḷaiyāvatallatu akamākāmai aṟika. ivvaruttam tīrum vāyilum uṇṭāyiṟṟu eṉpatām.
This is a comparison of the [subject]
[kuṟippu aṟital] kuṟippaṟitalāvatu, talaimakaḷ uḷḷak kuṟippiṉait talaimakaṉ aṟital.
[This section is called "Praise of the Deity"]—
(itaṉ poruḷ.) ivaḷ uṇ kaṇṇiluḷḷa nōkkam iraṇṭu vakaittu ; avviru vakaiyiṉum orunōkku nōy ceyyum ; orunōkku ataṟku maruntām enṟavāṟu.
The meaning of this [is as follows]
nōynōkkeṉpatu mutalnōkkiṉa nōkkam ; maruntunōkku eṉpatu itaṉāl varuttamuṟṟa talaimakaṉait talaimakaḷ uḷḷaṅkalaṅki nāṇōṭukūṭi nōkkiṉa nōkkam.
[Tiruvaḷḷuvar] has said that the primordial Lord is He who is the cause(?) of the world.
itu, nāṇamuṭaiya peṇṭiratu uḷḷakkaruttu veḷippaṭumāṟu kūṟiyatu.
[Tiruvaḷḷuvar] has said that the primordial Lord is He who is the cause(?) of the world.

[kuṟippu aṟital] kuṟippaṟitalāvatu, talaimakaḷ uḷḷak kuṟippiṉait talaimakaṉ aṟital. itu talaimakaṟkē urittu. peṇṭir nāṇamuṭaiyaraṉṟē! avaratu uḷḷakkaruttu veḷippaṭumāṟu eṉṉaiyeṉiṉ, mēlai atikārattut talaimakaṉaik kaṇṭa talamakaḷ, 'kāmam pōl kaṇtār makiḻceytal iṉṟu' (tirukkuṟal 1090) eṉṟu niṉaittāḷākak kūṟiṉāraṉṟē; ataṉāṉē kaṇṇum mukamum vēṟupaṭum; ataṉaṉē aṟiyalākum. maṉakkuṟippu aṟital kūṟiyatu eṟṟukku? piṟavāṟṟāṉuṅkūṭutaṟku neṟiyuḷavāleṉiṉ, piṟavāṟṟāṟ kūṭuṅkāl, kuravarāṟkūṭiṉ peruntiṇaiyām ; poruḷ koṭuttuc cāriṉ acuramām ; valiyiṟcāriṉ irākkatamām ; maṟaviyiṟ cāriṉ pacācamām ; ātaliṉ ikkūṭṭattukkuc kuṟippaṟintē puṇaravēṇṭutaliṉ itu kūṟappaṭṭatu. mēlataṉōṭu iyaipum itu. itu talaimakaṟku urittaṉṟēveṉiṉ avaṉ veḷippaṭa irattalāṉ vēṇṭā eṉka.
[This section is called "Praise of the Deity"]—
(itaṉ poruḷ.) ivaḷ maiyuṇ kaṇṇiluḷḷa nōkkam iraṇṭu vakaittu ; avviru vakaiyiṉum orunōkku nōy ceyyum ; orunōkku ataṟku maruntām enṟavāṟu.
The meaning of this [is as follows]
nōynōkkeṉpatu mutalnōkkiṉa nōkkam ; maruntunōkku eṉpatu itaṉāl varuttamuṟṟa talaimakaṉait talaimakaḷ uḷḷaṅkalaṅki nāṇōṭukūṭi nōkkiṉa nōkkam.
[Tiruvaḷḷuvar] has said that the primordial Lord is He who is the cause(?) of the world.
ataṉāṉē uṭampāṭu kāṇṭaliṉ maruntāyiṟṟu. itu, naṇinōkkutal uṭampaṭutalām eṉṟatu.
[Tiruvaḷḷuvar] has said that the primordial Lord is He who is the cause(?) of the world.
(itaṉ poruḷ.) iraṇṭu pārvai uṇṭu nāyakikku: orupārvai virakam tarum ; orupārvai virakattukku maruntākiya amutapārvai koṭukkum eṉṟavāṟu.
[Tiruvaḷḷuvar] has said that the primordial Lord is He who is the cause(?) of the world.

(itaṉ poruḷ.) neñcamē! ivaḷatu maiyuṇṭā kaṇṇiṉkaṇ uḷatākiya nōkkuttāṉ nampāl iraṇṭu nōkkāyiruntatu. iktu eṅṅaṉam eṉil, oru nōkkunam iṭarceyyum nōkkam ; oru nōkkam maṟṟu avviṭaṟ taṇittaṟku oru taṇimaruntu pōlum eṉṟavāṟu. eṉavē eṅkum ōṭumpōtu nōkkiṉ, taṉakku oru payaṉ iṉmaiyiṉ nōyatu eṉṟum. iṉit taṉvayiṟceṉṟa nōkkut taṉatu uyir āṟṟaṟkōr taṇṇaḷi ākaiyāl iṭartaṇi nōkku eṉṟum iṅṅaṉam ivaḷnōkkiṉaip pirittukkoṇṭu avaḷ uṭkuṟippu aṟintāṉ eṉpatu karuttu eṉṟavāṟu.
[Tiruvaḷḷuvar] has said that the primordial Lord is He who is the cause(?) of the world.
